usageNotes: Use this to obtain a SPICE connection ticket for a running QEMU VM; the returned object (host, password, tls-port, type, proxy) is passed directly to a SPICE client such as `remote-viewer`. The VM must be in a running state on the target node, and the caller needs `VM.Console` on `/vms/{vmid}`. Optionally pass the `proxy` field to override which cluster node the SPICE client should tunnel through — defaulting to the VM's current host is usually correct for direct access, but specifying the API node address improves reliability behind NAT.

examples.summary: Get SPICE config for VM 105 on node pve1, using the API node as the proxy

tips: The returned `password` is a one-time ticket valid for a short window — launch the SPICE client immediately after receiving it.
Pass the entire response object to `remote-viewer` via a .vv file or stdin; all required fields (host, tls-port, type, proxy, password) are included in the response.
Every Proxmox node runs `spiceproxy`, so any node in the cluster can serve as the proxy — pick the one closest to your client or the one you're already using for API calls.
SPICE requires the VM to have a SPICE display device configured (type: spice in the display options); VMs using VNC will not respond here.
API tokens are supported (`allowtoken: true`), so this call can be made from automation without a full user session.
